newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels free one hostage - live television.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels free one hostage - live television.

text.p: Marxist rebels holding VIP hostages inside the Japanese ambassador's home released a captive late on Sunday, live television pictures showed.

The release at 12.55 a.m. (0555 GMT) -- the first since Jan. 17 -- was believed to be on medical grounds and reduced to 72 the number of hostages held by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels.

The hostage left the residence on a stretcher accompanied by Red Cross representative Michel Minnig and Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani -- both members of the "guarantor commission" set up to oversee peace talks between the rebels and government.
The hostage, who was taken to an ambulance and driven away from the scene, was not immediately identified.

Late on Saturday, shouts were heard from within the residence calling for officials from the Red Cross to enter, witnesses said. Subsequently Red Cross officials entered the building with medical equipment, while an ambulance waited nearby, they added.

The rebels originally took more than 500 hostages on Dec. 17 during a cocktail party at the diplomatic mansion but have freed most of them. The remaining captives in the mined and booby-trapped residence include top Peruvian officials and Japanese diplomats and businessmen.
